Mide cuánto cambia la cantidad demandada: It measures how much the quantity demanded changes, in %, when the price changes by 1 %: $ε = (ΔQ/Q)/(ΔP/P)$. It is negative (when the price rises less is bought), and its absolute value is what is discussed: if $|ε| > 1$ demand is elastic, if $|ε| < 1$ inelastic and if $|ε| = 1$ unit elastic. Goods with few substitutes or that are very necessary, such as gasoline or electricity, have inelastic demand.
Si las variaciones se calculan sobre el: If the changes are computed relative to the initial value, the result depends on the direction of the change. The midpoint method divides by the average of the two values, $ε = (ΔQ/Q_m)/(ΔP/P_m)$, and gives the same result in both directions.
Con demanda elástica, subir el precio ba: With elastic demand, raising the price lowers revenue (many sales are lost); with inelastic demand, it raises it. On a linear demand curve the elasticity changes along the line and revenue is at its maximum exactly where it equals −1.
La elasticidad renta, $(ΔQ/Q)/(ΔR/R)$, d: Income elasticity, $(ΔQ/Q)/(ΔR/R)$, distinguishes normal goods (positive: necessities if less than 1, luxuries if greater) from inferior goods (negative). Cross elasticity, $(ΔQ_x/Q_x)/(ΔP_y/P_y)$, is positive for substitutes (coffee and tea) and negative for complements (cars and gasoline).
